sources.title: Self-pollination in island and mainland populations of the introduced hummingbird-pollinated plant, Nicotiana glauca (Solanaceae)
measured_links: pollen removal and stigma pollen deposition
open intact versus open emasculated reproductive-assurance test

sampling_notes.autogamy: 1998 CAT n=18 plants, SED n=11, STA n=12; 1999 CRU n=9 and STA n=9
sampling_notes.pollen_limitation: 1998 CAT n=24, SED n=11, STA n=12; 1999 CRU n=10, CAT n=17, STA n=13
sampling_notes.emasculation: paired treatments on at least 10 plants at CAT, SED and STA in spring 1998, STA again summer 1998, and CRU summer 1999
sampling_notes.pollen_transfer: five flowers per plant for at least six plants per site; CRU and STA in Nov 1999 and CRU, CAT, STA and MON in Jun 2000

source_native_results.visitation: No statistically detectable island decrease in visitation frequency or increase in temporal/spatial variability.
source_native_results.pollen_transfer: Pollen transfer was not lower on islands; CRU stigma pollen deposition exceeded STA in Nov 1999, and June 2000 site tests also did not support reduced island service.
source_native_results.pollen_limitation: Island fruit set was not pollen limited in 1998 or 1999; mainland sites were pollen limited in 1998 but not 1999.
source_native_results.reproductive_assurance: Open emasculation reduced fruit set significantly at STA in one season and tended to at SED, but not CAT or CRU; island-mainland treatment-effect difference P=0.063.
source_native_results.selfing_capacity: Island populations had higher autonomous self-pollination capacity, strongest on recently colonized CRU.

sources.title: Island-mainland difference in Nicotiana glauca (Solanaceae) corolla length: a product of pollinator-mediated selection?
measured_links: phenotypic selection using pollen transfer, fruit set and seed count
single-visit hummingbird pollen deposition and removal at CAT and STA
supplemental hand-pollination control for non-pollinator fecundity effects

source_native_numeric_anchors.morphology_sampling: at least 10 one-day-old flowers per plant from 15-30 plants per population; CAT 30, CRU 20, SED 20, STA 15; 166-230 flowers per site
source_native_numeric_anchors.island_corolla_difference: approximately 1 mm longer on islands on average
source_native_numeric_anchors.single_visit_design: sets of 20 tagged flowers; repeated for 3 days for two sets at CAT and five at STA; at least six Allen's and three Anna's hummingbirds at CAT and at least two Anna's at STA
source_native_numeric_anchors.phenotypic_selection_pairs: CAT versus STA spring 1999, CRU versus STA fall 1999, CAT versus MON summer 2000
source_native_numeric_anchors.per_visit_result: Allen's hummingbirds deposited and removed significantly less pollen per visit than Anna's, but per-visit effectiveness was not associated with corolla length

cross_source_linkage.same_site_year_effectiveness_anchor: The 2007 single-visit experiment is CAT and STA in June 2000; the 2004 source also contains June 2000 pollen-transfer sampling including CAT and STA, strengthening same-system/site-year linkage for the service component.
cross_source_linkage.why_partial_not_complete: The studies share named populations and overlapping study years, and together cover floral response, pollinator effectiveness/service, and reproductive dependency/assurance. However, the current source record does not establish that the floral, per-visit, pollen-limitation, autogamy and emasculation experiments used the same tagged plants, reproductive-dependency experiments were primarily in 1998-1999 rather than the June 2000 per-visit window, and stable source bytes for the two declared articles remain unrecovered.
cross_source_linkage.allowed_claim: This system supplies a genuine partial mechanistic bridge and a strong alternative-mechanism test: current island pollinator service did not explain the stronger selfing capacity, making colonization/establishment filtering a live mechanism rather than assuming post-establishment pollinator scarcity.
blocked_claims: do not call this a complete causal chain
do not infer historical selection from current contrasts
do not treat self-compatibility alone as effective dependency
do not pool the 2004 and 2007 measurements as if they were the same individual-level observations
do not admit unlocked numeric discoveries into the formal cross-system effect registry
do not admit a cross-system effect size until source-native numeric estimates, uncertainty, hierarchy and provenance are locked
